metadata.case_name: DHILLON CHAMKAUR SINGH v. YIU SZE YUEN

source: X-ray of left ankle showed fracture of lateral malleolus.
The diagnosis was fracture of left ankle lateral malleolus.
X-ray of his left ankle showed fracture of left lateral malleolus.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

manifestations.description: tenderness and swelling over medial and lateral aspect of left ankle
severe pain in left foot; pain would increase whenever he walked or stood for 10 minutes and would radiate with climbing on stairs
could not stand on his left foot
required 2 elbow crutches and was taught left non-weight bearing walking
could not climb stairs for more than 9 to 10 steps without resting for 1 to 2 minutes
pain affects his sleep; spent most time in bed
mild residual pain today that requires him to seek symptomatic relief of painkiller prescribed to him

losses.description: Could not stand or walk without 2 crutches for several months after the Accident; non-weight bearing walking and limitation on climbing stairs
Had to rely on his friends for daily activities e.g. asking them to buy daily food and household products for him, and asking them to cook for him

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Used to enjoy playing cricket with friends but he could not resume it given his conditions

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Required help from friends for buying food and household products and for cooking

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Sik Pan v Wylam’s Service Ltd & Others
Li Chi Sing v Equal Link Ltd
comparable_cases.injury_description: received open reduction and internal fixation with plate and screws; left with an 11-cm scar; 14 sessions of physiotherapy; total sick leave of 166 days; good recovery

comparable_cases.case_name: Lam Kam Fai v Yau Shing Scaffolding Co Ltd & Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: fractured left distal fibula requiring surgery; walked with crutches for some 9 months; 4-month physiotherapy; later readmitted for 6 days for removal of implants; walked unaided and full recovery afterwards

comparable_cases.case_name: Ching Yuk Yee v Furniss Jacqueline Elizabeth & Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: open reduction and internal fixation for left ankle fracture, and later an implant removal operation; also diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder and depression

comparable_cases.case_name: Tamang Tikaram v Tong Kee Company Limited & Others
comparable_cases.injury_description: minimally displaced fracture of right medial malleolus; no operation; given a short leg dynast (worn for 7 weeks); hospitalized for 3 days; attended 19 sessions of physiotherapy and 17 sessions of occupational therapy; could walk without aid; no scar or deformity; reduced range of motion

comparable_cases.case_name: Tsui Wai Ho v Pride Glory Limited trading as Ziti’s
comparable_cases.injury_description: fractured distal fibula, requiring open reduction and internal fixation, 7 follow-ups, 13 sessions of physiotherapy and occupational therapy, operation for implant removal; fracture healed well with satisfactory range of movement; full recovery achieved 2 years after accident
